seo_description: CutoutDropZone is a free, open-source Mac app that removes photo backgrounds offline with Apple Vision. Drop images, get transparent PNG cutouts.
hero_sub: Drop one image or a whole batch and get a transparent-background cutout of the subject, made offline with Apple's Vision framework. Press Space to flip between before and after.
features_sub: Everything runs on your Mac, from subject detection to export.

features.title: Subject lifting with Vision
features.desc: Uses Apple's foreground instance mask to separate the subject from the background. Large images are downscaled for the model and the mask is scaled back up.

features.title: Batch queue and drop zone
features.desc: Drop PNG, JPEG, HEIC or TIFF files, or whole folders, onto the window or the Dock icon. Images are processed in the background with per-image progress, and bad files do not stop the batch.

features.title: Per-image controls
features.desc: Choose a transparent, white, black or custom background, set an edge feather from 0 to 5 px, and trim to the subject bounds. Click a subject in the preview to include or exclude it.

features.title: Before and after preview
features.desc: Compare the original and the cutout on a checkerboard, toggled with the Space bar.

features.title: Export, copy or drag out
features.desc: Save PNG with transparency or JPEG, export everything to a folder with a suffix like -cutout, copy to the clipboard, or drag a cutout straight into Finder. Originals are never overwritten.

features.title: Private and offline
features.desc: No network calls, no analytics and no third-party dependencies. Your photos never leave your Mac.

faq.q: Is CutoutDropZone free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is free to use and released under the MIT license, with the full source on GitHub. If it saves you time, there is an optional Support / Donate button in the app.

None beyond the standard macOS panels. It reads only the images you drop or choose, and writes to the output folder you pick. It does not ask for Accessibility, Screen Recording, Camera or Microphone access.

Your images stay where they are, and cutouts are saved to the folder you choose in Settings. Temporary files for drag-out and for images dropped from browsers live in ~/Library/Caches/CutoutDropZone and are cleared on the next launch.

Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, and this is a free project. Right-click the app and choose Open once to get past Gatekeeper, or build it yourself from source with Xcode and XcodeGen.
